title: Fish Rundown
subtitle: Caribbean fish simmered in reduced coconut milk with scotch bonnet and thyme
excerpt: White fish simmered in coconut milk cooked down until thick and oily, with scotch bonnet, spring onion and thyme. Rundown refers to the reducing of the coconut milk. Serve with boiled dumplings or green banana.
sourceNotes: Rundown is a Jamaican dish where coconut milk is boiled down until it separates into a thick, oily sauce. The technique appears across Caribbean cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The coconut sauce can be prepared up to a day ahead and stored in the fridge. Add the fish fresh when reheating.

content.text: Rundown takes patience. The coconut milk must reduce until it thickens and the oil separates before the fish goes in. Rush this stage and the sauce will be thin and watery rather than rich and coating.
Toss the fish pieces with lemon juice, salt and pepper. Set aside while you prepare the sauce.
Pour the coconut milk into a large saucepan. Bring to the boil over a medium-high heat.
Boil the coconut milk for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Watch for the point when the milk thickens and the oil begins to separate at the surface. This is the rundown.
Add the onion, spring onion, garlic, scotch bonnet, thyme and allspice. Cook for 3 minutes in the thickened coconut milk.
Add the tomatoes and green pepper. Stir and cook for 2 minutes.
Gently lay the fish pieces into the sauce. Spoon the sauce over the top.
Reduce the heat to low. Cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily. Remove the scotch bonnet and thyme stalks before serving.

items.symptom: The coconut milk did not thicken or separate.
items.cause: The heat was too low or the tin was low-fat coconut milk.
items.fix: Use full-fat coconut milk only. Increase the heat and continue boiling. The separation can take up to 25 minutes.

items.symptom: The fish has broken into small pieces.
items.cause: The fish was stirred too much or added before the sauce was ready.
items.fix: Place the fish gently and spoon sauce over the top rather than stirring. Leave it undisturbed while it cooks.

items.symptom: The sauce is too rich and oily.
items.cause: The coconut milk was reduced too far before the fish went in.
items.fix: Add a splash of water to loosen the sauce and stir gently before serving.
